# Tool catalog

<!-- Generated by `python scripts/generate_tool_catalog.py`. Do not edit by hand: a test fails when this file is out of date. -->

Every tool the server can offer, in plain language. The **Tool ID** is the stable name that applications and policies use; the **title** is only what a person sees. A title, a category or a read-only label is information for the application, not permission: what a tool may do is decided by the server, and for a broker client by its policy.

## How to read it

- **Effect:** *Reads only* tools change nothing on the NAS. *Changes things* tools write. *Deletes data* tools remove something this server cannot bring back.
- **Sign-in needed:** with manual authentication, you sign in yourself on the private page. A tool that needs it answers `AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED` until you have. The AI application never receives your NAS password or one-time code.
- **On by default:** *Yes* means a default installation (restricted mode) offers the tool **and** a broker client has it in its default grant. *Restricted mode only* means a default installation offers it but a broker client has to be given it in its policy. *No* means it has to be turned on, as described below.
- **Contents go to the AI provider:** anything a tool returns is seen by the AI application and its provider. Tools marked this way return free text or file content you may not have read, so ask for only what is needed.

### Turning a tool on

- **Restricted mode** is on by default and offers only browsing and monitoring tools, plus sign-in and sign-out. Setting `RESTRICTED_MODE=false` makes every registered tool available: the tools that change things, and also the account and permission tools. Those only read, but a list of every account is a different level of trust from a list of files, so they are off in restricted mode.
- **A broker client** gets the tools in its policy entry (`tools`), or the default set marked below if it has none. A tool must be allowed by *both* the policy and the broker's restricted mode: to give a client a tool that changes things, the broker needs `RESTRICTED_MODE=false` as well as the tool in that client's entry. `synology_login` can never be granted.

## Connection

| Title | Tool ID | What it does | Effect | Sign-in needed | On by default |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Connection status | `synology_status` | Shows which configured NAS units are signed in. It never signs anyone in. | Reads only | No | Yes |
| Configured NAS units | `synology_list_nas` | Lists the NAS units this server knows about, with their addresses and whether each is signed in. | Reads only | No | Yes |
| Sign in (legacy mode only) | `synology_login` | Signs in with a username and password given in the call. It exists only in legacy mode: with manual authentication it is not offered at all, because a password must never pass through an AI application. The user signs in on the private page instead. Needs `base_url`, `username`, `password`. Legacy mode only. | Changes things | No | Legacy mode only |
| Sign out | `synology_logout` | Ends the session with a NAS. Signing in again is done by the user. Needs `base_url`. | Changes things | No | Yes |

Safe examples (the arguments of one call):

- `synology_status`: `{}`
- `synology_list_nas`: `{}`
- `synology_logout`: `{"base_url": "https://nas.example:5001"}`

## Health and monitoring

| Title | Tool ID | What it does | Effect | Sign-in needed | On by default |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| System information | `synology_system_info` | Model, serial number, DSM version, uptime and temperature. | Reads only | Yes | Yes |
| CPU and memory use | `synology_utilization` | Current CPU, memory, swap and disk activity. | Reads only | Yes | Yes |
| Disk health | `synology_disk_health` | Every physical disk with its S.M.A.R.T. status, model, temperature and capacity. | Reads only | Yes | Yes |
| Disk S.M.A.R.T. details | `synology_disk_smart` | The detailed S.M.A.R.T. attributes of one disk. Needs `disk_id`. | Reads only | Yes | Yes |
| Volume status | `synology_volume_status` | Every volume with its status, size, space used and RAID type. | Reads only | Yes | Yes |
| Storage pools | `synology_storage_pool` | Every storage pool with its RAID level, status and member disks. | Reads only | Yes | Yes |
| Network status | `synology_network` | Network interfaces with their status and current transfer rates. | Reads only | Yes | Yes |
| UPS status | `synology_ups` | The uninterruptible power supply: status, battery level and power. | Reads only | Yes | Yes |
| Installed packages | `synology_services` | The installed packages and whether each is running. | Reads only | Yes | Yes |
| System log | `synology_system_log` | Recent system log entries. They can contain user names and file names. Contents go to the AI provider. | Reads only | Yes | Restricted mode only |
| NAS health summary | `synology_health_summary` | One overview of system, CPU and memory, disks, volumes, storage pools, network and UPS, and which checks could not be completed. | Reads only | Yes | Yes |

Safe examples (the arguments of one call):

- `synology_system_info`: `{"nas_name": "nas1"}`
- `synology_utilization`: `{"nas_name": "nas1"}`
- `synology_disk_health`: `{"nas_name": "nas1"}`
- `synology_disk_smart`: `{"nas_name": "nas1", "disk_id": "sata1"}`
- `synology_volume_status`: `{"nas_name": "nas1"}`
- `synology_storage_pool`: `{"nas_name": "nas1"}`
- `synology_network`: `{"nas_name": "nas1"}`
- `synology_ups`: `{"nas_name": "nas1"}`
- `synology_services`: `{"nas_name": "nas1"}`
- `synology_system_log`: `{"nas_name": "nas1"}`
- `synology_health_summary`: `{"nas_name": "nas1"}`

## Files

| Title | Tool ID | What it does | Effect | Sign-in needed | On by default |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Browse shared folders | `list_shares` | Lists the shared folders on a NAS. With manual authentication, only the shares this client may reach are shown. | Reads only | Yes | Yes |
| List a folder | `list_directory` | Lists what is inside a folder, with type, size and dates. Needs `path`. | Reads only | Yes | Yes |
| File details | `get_file_info` | Size, dates and type of one file or folder. Says plainly when it does not exist. Needs `path`. | Reads only | Yes | Yes |
| Search files | `search_files` | Finds files and folders whose names match a pattern, inside one folder. A search of a large folder can take a while and is stopped at its time limit. Needs `path`, `pattern`. | Reads only | Yes | Yes |
| Read a file | `get_file_content` | The text of one file. The content goes to the AI application and its provider. Files over the size limit (1,000,000 bytes unless MAX_FILE_CONTENT_SIZE says otherwise) are refused. Needs `path`. Contents go to the AI provider. | Reads only | Yes | Yes |
| Rename a file or folder | `rename_file` | Gives one file or folder a new name, in the same place. Needs `path`, `new_name`. | Changes things | Yes | No |
| Move a file or folder | `move_file` | Moves a file or folder to another folder. Needs `source_path`, `destination_path`. | Changes things | Yes | No |
| Create a file | `create_file` | Creates a new file with the text it is given. Needs `path`. | Changes things | Yes | No |
| Create a folder | `create_directory` | Creates a new folder inside an existing one. Needs `folder_path`, `name`. | Changes things | Yes | No |
| Delete a file or folder | `delete` | Deletes a file, or a folder and everything in it. This server cannot undo it. Needs `path`. | Deletes data | Yes | No |

Safe examples (the arguments of one call):

- `list_shares`: `{"nas_name": "nas1"}`
- `list_directory`: `{"nas_name": "nas1", "path": "/Shared/Documents"}`
- `get_file_info`: `{"nas_name": "nas1", "path": "/Shared/Documents/report.txt"}`
- `search_files`: `{"nas_name": "nas1", "path": "/Shared/Documents", "pattern": "*.pdf"}`
- `get_file_content`: `{"nas_name": "nas1", "path": "/Shared/Documents/notes.txt"}`

## Downloads

| Title | Tool ID | What it does | Effect | Sign-in needed | On by default |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Download Station settings | `ds_get_info` | Download Station's version and settings. | Reads only | Yes | Restricted mode only |
| List downloads | `ds_list_tasks` | Every download in Download Station with its status. | Reads only | Yes | Restricted mode only |
| Start a download | `ds_create_task` | Adds a download from a web address or a magnet link. Needs `uri`. Through the adapter, leave out `password`: the adapter refuses a call that carries a field named like a credential. | Changes things | Yes | No |
| Pause downloads | `ds_pause_tasks` | Pauses one or more downloads. Needs `task_ids`. | Changes things | Yes | No |
| Resume downloads | `ds_resume_tasks` | Resumes one or more paused downloads. Needs `task_ids`. | Changes things | Yes | No |
| Remove downloads | `ds_delete_tasks` | Removes one or more downloads from Download Station. Needs `task_ids`. | Deletes data | Yes | No |
| Download speeds | `ds_get_statistics` | Current download and upload speeds. | Reads only | Yes | Restricted mode only |
| List downloaded files | `ds_list_downloaded_files` | The files in Download Station's destination folder. | Reads only | Yes | Restricted mode only |

Safe examples (the arguments of one call):

- `ds_get_info`: `{"nas_name": "nas1"}`
- `ds_list_tasks`: `{"nas_name": "nas1"}`
- `ds_get_statistics`: `{"nas_name": "nas1"}`
- `ds_list_downloaded_files`: `{"nas_name": "nas1"}`

## Containers

| Title | Tool ID | What it does | Effect | Sign-in needed | On by default |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| List containers | `synology_container_list` | Every Container Manager container with its status. | Reads only | Yes | Yes |

| Delete a container | `synology_container_delete` | Deletes a container. Needs `name`. | Deletes data | Yes | No |

| Container resource use | `synology_container_resource` | Current CPU and memory use of one container. Needs `name`. | Reads only | Yes | Yes |
| List projects | `synology_container_project_list` | Every Container Manager project with its status. | Reads only | Yes | Yes |
| Project details | `synology_container_project_get` | One project, including its compose file, which can hold environment variables and secrets. Needs `name`. Contents go to the AI provider. | Reads only | Yes | Restricted mode only |
| Create a project | `synology_container_project_create` | Creates a project from a compose file. Needs `name`, `share_path`, `content`. | Changes things | Yes | No |
| Update a project | `synology_container_project_update` | Replaces a project's compose file. Needs `name`, `content`. | Changes things | Yes | No |
| Start a project | `synology_container_project_start` | Starts a project. Needs `name`. | Changes things | Yes | No |
| Stop a project | `synology_container_project_stop` | Stops a project. Needs `name`. | Changes things | Yes | No |
| Restart a project | `synology_container_project_restart` | Restarts a project. Needs `name`. | Changes things | Yes | No |
| Build a project | `synology_container_project_build` | Builds a project. Needs `name`. | Changes things | Yes | No |
| Clean a project | `synology_container_project_clean` | Cleans up a project's containers and images. Needs `name`. | Changes things | Yes | No |
| Delete a project | `synology_container_project_delete` | Deletes a project. Needs `name`. | Deletes data | Yes | No |
| List images | `synology_container_image_list` | Every container image on the NAS. | Reads only | Yes | Yes |
| Image details | `synology_container_image_get` | One image, including how it was built. Needs `name`. | Reads only | Yes | Restricted mode only |
| Delete an image | `synology_container_image_delete` | Deletes an image. Needs `name`. | Deletes data | Yes | No |
| Pull an image | `synology_container_image_pull` | Downloads an image from a registry to the NAS. Needs `repository`. | Changes things | Yes | No |
| List image registries | `synology_container_registry_list` | The registries Container Manager can pull from. | Reads only | Yes | Yes |
| Search image registries | `synology_container_registry_search` | Searches the registries for an image. Needs `query`. | Reads only | Yes | Yes |
| List image tags | `synology_container_registry_tags` | The tags available for one registry image. Needs `repository`. | Reads only | Yes | Yes |
| Download a registry image | `synology_container_registry_download` | Downloads an image from a registry to the NAS. Needs `repository`. | Changes things | Yes | No |
| List container networks | `synology_container_network_list` | Every container network. | Reads only | Yes | Yes |
| Network details | `synology_container_network_get` | One container network. Needs `name`. | Reads only | Yes | Yes |
| Create a container network | `synology_container_network_create` | Creates a container network. Needs `name`. | Changes things | Yes | No |
| Delete a container network | `synology_container_network_delete` | Deletes a container network. Needs `name`. | Deletes data | Yes | No |

## Sharing and NFS

| Title | Tool ID | What it does | Effect | Sign-in needed | On by default |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| NFS status | `synology_nfs_status` | Whether the NFS file service is on, and its settings. | Reads only | Yes | Yes |
| Turn NFS on or off | `synology_nfs_enable` | Turns the NFS file service on or off. | Changes things | Yes | No |
| NFS access by folder | `synology_nfs_list_shares` | Every shared folder with the NFS access it allows. | Reads only | Yes | Yes |
| Set NFS access | `synology_nfs_set_permission` | Sets which client addresses may use a shared folder over NFS, and how. Needs `share_name`, `client_ip`. | Changes things | Yes | No |
| Create a shared folder | `synology_create_share` | Creates a new shared folder on a volume. Needs `share_name`, `vol_path`. | Changes things | Yes | No |

Safe examples (the arguments of one call):

- `synology_nfs_status`: `{"nas_name": "nas1"}`
- `synology_nfs_list_shares`: `{"nas_name": "nas1"}`

## Users and groups

| Title | Tool ID | What it does | Effect | Sign-in needed | On by default |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| List users | `synology_list_users` | Every local user. | Reads only | Yes | No |
| User details | `synology_get_user` | Details of one local user. Needs `name`. | Reads only | Yes | No |
| Create a user | `synology_create_user` | Creates a local user. It takes a password for the new account. Needs `name`, `password`. Cannot be used through the adapter: it needs `password`, `cannot_chg_passwd`, `passwd_never_expire`, and the adapter refuses a call that carries a field named like a credential. | Changes things | Yes | No |
| Change a user | `synology_set_user` | Renames a user, changes a password, or enables or disables the account. Needs `name`. Through the adapter, leave out `password`: the adapter refuses a call that carries a field named like a credential. | Changes things | Yes | No |
| Delete a user | `synology_delete_user` | Deletes a local user. Needs `name`. | Deletes data | Yes | No |
| List groups | `synology_list_groups` | Every local group. | Reads only | Yes | No |
| Group members | `synology_list_group_members` | The members of one group. Needs `group`. | Reads only | Yes | No |
| Add a user to groups | `synology_add_user_to_group` | Adds a user to one or more groups. Needs `username`, `groups`. | Changes things | Yes | No |
| Remove a user from groups | `synology_remove_user_from_group` | Removes a user from one or more groups. Needs `username`, `groups`. | Changes things | Yes | No |
| User folder permissions | `synology_get_user_permissions` | Which shared folders a user may read or write. Needs `name`. | Reads only | Yes | No |
| Set user folder permissions | `synology_set_user_permissions` | Sets, per shared folder, whether a user may read, write or is denied. Needs `name`, `permissions`. | Changes things | Yes | No |
